solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Angry about being corralled by one with even stricter diet than me (10)

indicators.note: the word for angry turns round
the turned word is penned inside the other

blocks.note: a vegan eats no animal products at all

annotation.surface: A cross vegetarian grumbles at being hemmed in by a vegan.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word: 'me' is the vegetarian speaking, so the whole clue is written from the answer's point of view.
annotation.definitionFit: The speaker's diet is only a little less strict than a vegan's, so the speaker is a vegetarian.

entries.clue: Shipwrecked heroine that may be found in bed (5)

definitions.text: that may be found in bed

blocks.note: the heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, washed ashore in Illyria

blocks.clueFragment: that may be found in bed
blocks.note: a garden flower of the violet family, grown in flower beds

annotation.surface: A castaway heroine turns up in someone's bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests a bedroom; it is a flower bed, which is where the second sense of the name grows.
annotation.definitionFit: Viola is the shipwrecked heroine of Twelfth Night, and violas are bedding plants.

entries.clue: One perhaps flying over grand, ancient hilltop (9)

blocks.note: the crest is the top of a hill

annotation.surface: Something soars over a grand old summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that the definition is an example: a goldcrest is one thing that flies.
annotation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is a tiny European songbird, one of many things that fly.

entries.clue: Oddball turning up part of nose properly over small town (9,5)

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for oddball is written upwards
in a down clue the earlier pieces sit above the last one

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A strange person pokes about at someone's nose above a little town.
annotation.walkthrough: Tunbridge Wells is a genteel spa town in Kent, England, long a byword for respectable middle-class indignation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Tunbridge Wells is one particular town, a spa town in Kent.

entries.clue: Reacting to oxygen in sport with sharp pain (7)

blocks.note: a sting is a sharp pain

annotation.surface: A player gasping for air mid-match feels a stab of pain.
annotation.walkthrough: Rusting is iron combining with oxygen, a chemistry definition dressed up as someone short of breath.
annotation.definitionFit: Iron rusts by reacting with oxygen and water.

entries.clue: Succeeded entering stadium, left side (7)

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded goes inside the stadium

blocks.note: S = succeeded, as in family trees

annotation.surface: Someone got in at the left side of a stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left side' looks like one phrase for a position; it splits into L and the definition. Arsenal is a London football club, so a side.
annotation.definitionFit: Arsenal is an English football team, and a team is a side.

entries.clue: I can’t tell you to succeed (4)

blocks.note: what a quiz contestant says when stumped
what you do in an exam when you succeed

annotation.surface: Someone refuses to reveal the secret of success.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is a whole spoken reply: 'Pass' is what you say when you don't know the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Pass' declines a question, and to pass is to succeed.

entries.clue: A win? Not once (5)

blocks.note: a profit or advantage is a win

annotation.surface: Someone asks if there was ever a victory and hears 'not once'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not once' reads as 'never'; here it means more than once, which is doing it again.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done a second time has happened more than once, so 'not once' is a playful synonym.

entries.clue: Emergency for journey to relieve ancient city (5,4)

blocks.note: to spare someone a task is to relieve them of it

annotation.surface: An urgent expedition sets out to lift the siege of an old city.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: the spare tyre is what you keep for a roadside emergency.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the kit you rely on when a puncture interrupts a drive.

entries.clue: In principal role, one part of body controls another (14)

blocks.note: the head is part of the body

annotation.surface: An actor in a lead part makes one part of the body direct another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Principal role' sounds theatrical; it is the job of a school's principal.
annotation.definitionFit: The principal of a British school is its head, so the principal role is that post.

entries.clue: Recent pupil pines for the quadrangles (7)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil

annotation.surface: A school leaver misses the quads of the old college.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quadrangles' suggests college courtyards; here it is the geometry sense, four-sided figures.
annotation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle, a four-sided figure or quadrangle.

entries.clue: In Yemeni capital ran across man of note (7)

indicators.note: the word for ran across goes inside the capital

blocks.note: Sana'a is the capital of Yemen

annotation.surface: In Sana'a, someone bumped into a distinguished figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yemeni capital' wants to be the letter Y; it is the whole city. 'Man of note' means a composer, a man of musical notes.
annotation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer, a man of musical note.

entries.clue: Current one working bearing string instrument (9)

indicators.note: the word for one working carries the string alongside, after it

blocks.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine

annotation.surface: A live wire runs through a working string instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'String instrument' reads as one phrase, but the string belongs to the wordplay and the definition is just 'instrument'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one member of the class of musical instruments, a squeezebox.

entries.clue: One capped once, career’s beginning to run into the sand (5)

indicators.note: take only the first letter of career
that letter goes inside the sand

blocks.note: a dune is a hill of sand

annotation.surface: A former international footballer sees his career run into the sand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capped' suggests a sporting cap; the dunce's cap was once put on slow pupils.
annotation.definitionFit: Dunces were once made to wear a conical dunce's cap.

entries.clue: Wanting too much golf, does have to step back (5)

definitions.note: the definition is a gerund phrase naming the vice; greed is that wanting

indicators.note: the word for does walks backwards

blocks.note: golf is G in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A golfer who plays too much must take a step back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as a verb; it is the plural of doe.
annotation.definitionFit: Greed is wanting more than you need.

entries.clue: Endlessly questioned about investment in painting (9)

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word is lopped off
the shortened word goes round the investment

blocks.note: an ISA is a British tax-free savings account

annotation.surface: Someone is interrogated without end about money sunk into a picture.
annotation.walkthrough: An ISA (Individual Savings Account) is a common British tax-free investment.
annotation.definitionFit: Grisaille is painting done entirely in shades of grey.

entries.clue: Almost all the time in Britain, yes? This isn’t (6,3)

indicators.note: almost all of the word is used: everything but its last letter
the shortened word sits inside the letters for Britain

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether it is nearly always like this in Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: GB is part of the answer, yet Galway Bay is in Ireland, so 'this' is not in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Galway Bay lies on the west coast of Ireland, not in Britain.

entries.clue: British: why they can’t swim in resort? (9)

annotation.surface: Someone explains why the British can't swim at the seaside.
annotation.walkthrough: Blackpool is a traditional English seaside resort in Lancashire; the question mark flags the fanciful reason.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one particular English seaside resort, famous for its tower and piers.

entries.clue: Cook lunch: I bet one so needs food for two? (2,3,4)

definitions.text: one so needs food for two
definitions.note: the clue describes a woman who is 'so', i.e. in the club, rather than giving a synonym

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up like ingredients

annotation.surface: A cook bets that a mother-to-be must be eating for two.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant, and a pregnant woman is said to be eating for two.
annotation.definitionFit: A woman in the club is pregnant, so she is eating for two.

entries.clue: Not be honest about alcoholic drink and soft one (7)

indicators.note: the word for not be honest goes round the drink

blocks.note: to lie is not to be honest

annotation.surface: Someone fibs about the hard stuff and a soft drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' in 'soft one' stands for the drink just mentioned, so the definition is a soft drink.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Soft one' stands for a soft drink, and this lime-flavoured non-alcoholic drink is an example.

entries.clue: 50s child eating large loaf (7)

indicators.note: the child takes the L inside

blocks.note: a baby boomer, born in the postwar baby boom

annotation.surface: A child of the fifties tucks into a big loaf.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British bread loaf with diagonal slashes across its top.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one kind of British bread loaf, long with slashes across the top.

entries.clue: Scottish title compared with English (5)

annotation.surface: A Scottish rank is weighed against its English equal.
annotation.walkthrough: A thane was a Scottish noble, as in Macbeth, Thane of Cawdor.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one rank of the old Scottish nobility, as held by Macbeth.

entries.clue: Heading off, risk walk (5)

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to gamble is to risk; drop the G

annotation.surface: Setting off, someone chances a walk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like leaving; it tells you to take the head off the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with a leisurely pace built in.

entries.clue: Confused situation of black murder victim (5)

blocks.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

annotation.surface: A detective tries to make sense of a muddled crime scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tower of Babel is where languages were confused, so a babel is a noisy muddle.
annotation.definitionFit: From the Tower of Babel, where tongues were confused, the name became a common noun for any confused scene.

entries.clue: Ark struggling with no more sail (9)

indicators.note: the letters thrash about into a new order

annotation.surface: Noah's ark is in difficulty, with no sail left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sail' reads as a verb; it is a noun, a small sail set above the skysail on a square-rigger.
annotation.definitionFit: A moonraker is a light topmost sail on a square-rigged ship.

entries.clue: Hindu themes initially appearing in lesser newspapers (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of appearing
that letter goes inside the newspapers

annotation.surface: Hindu subjects start turning up in the tabloids.
annotation.walkthrough: A raga is a melodic framework of Indian classical music, a theme in the musical sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Ragas are the melodic themes of Indian classical music.

entries.clue: At first look daggers at a bloomer (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of look

blocks.note: an obelus is the dagger symbol † used in printing

annotation.surface: Someone glares at another person who has made a blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a blunder, and 'look daggers' as glaring; the bloomer is a plant in bloom.
annotation.definitionFit: A lobelia is a flowering plant, something that blooms.

entries.clue: Game John edited in periodical (3-4)

indicators.note: the name's letters are rearranged
the rearranged name goes inside the periodical

annotation.surface: A magazine article about a game has been revised by John.
annotation.walkthrough: The periodical is split around the scrambled name, not placed next to it.
annotation.definitionFit: Mah-jong is a Chinese game played with tiles.

entries.clue: Like a fish, very hard? No way (4)

indicators.note: the word for way is taken away

blocks.note: ST = street, a way; it is removed

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a fish is really tough and is told no way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No way' reads as a flat denial; it is an instruction to remove ST from STEELY.
annotation.definitionFit: Eely means like an eel, a fish, and so slippery.

entries.clue: Implores to move to city (10)

indicators.note: the letters change places

annotation.surface: Someone begs to relocate to the big city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Implores' alone is two letters short; the 'to' after it belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a sense of scale: the word, Greek for mother city, means a chief or very large city.
